title: Best-improved supplier, worst-performing valve
setting: Brenmoor Heat Systems (fictional) builds AH-series air-source heat pumps, about 4,100 units a month. In January 2026 it launched SupplierPath, a supplier-quality programme that scores suppliers each quarter and grants dock-to-stock status (no receiving inspection) at a score of 85 or more. The VA-220 four-way reversing valve comes from Pellacott Precision (about 80% of volume) and Durrant-Hale Components (20%). Pellacott's score rose from 70 to 89 and it reached dock-to-stock in July 2026. Over the same period, field claims coded to the VA-220 rose sharply. Brenmoor also onboarded 14 new installer firms in early 2026 and rolled out controller firmware 4.2 in March.
presentingRequest: The COO asks: why have VA-220 field failures risen while Pellacott's SupplierPath score improved, and what should Brenmoor do now, including about the six Pellacott lots receiving has on hold?

initialEvidence.source: Email from Marcus Ilvane, VP Operations, to quality leadership, 12 Oct 2026
initialEvidence.text: Subject: VA-220 claims. Let's not chase the wrong rabbit. Pellacott is our best-improved supplier: SupplierPath score 70 to 89, dock-to-stock since July, every lot certified 100% leak-tested. What changed on our side this year is 14 new installer firms and firmware 4.2. Field service already tells me the new firms' jobs are where the failures are. Receiving put six Pellacott lots on hold on 1 October, and that means a line stoppage next week. Pellacott has offered fresh certificates for those lots; once they arrive, release them. I want an installer remediation plan by Friday.

VA-220-coded claims within 120 days in service, per 1,000 units, by build month: 2025 average 6; Jan 2026 22; Feb 30; Mar 33; Apr 35; May 34; Jun 21 (120-day window incomplete). Top 2026 claim code: 'reversing valve – capacity loss / internal leak' (82% of VA-220 claims). VA-220 sources in 2026: Pellacott about 80% of volume, Durrant-Hale about 20%. The dashboard does not split claims by valve source, installer or firmware version.

Score = 0.45 × on-site process audit + 0.40 × submitted test-record conformance + 0.15 × delivery. Test-record conformance = percentage of lot certificates that carry complete per-piece leak values with every piece within the stated limit. Dock-to-stock is granted automatically at 85 or above. Q4 2025 baseline: 74 / 58 (per-piece leak values missing on 9 of 14 certificates) / 88 = 70. Q1 2026 (document review 31 Mar): 76 / 92 / 88 = 84. Q2 (2 Jul): 78 / 100 / 90 = 89, dock-to-stock granted. Q3 (30 Sep): 79 / 100 / 90 = 89. Programme note: across all 22 SupplierPath suppliers, average test-record conformance went from 71 (Q4 2025) to 96 (Q3 2026).

initialEvidence.source: Pellacott Precision process change notice PCN-25-118, 2 Dec 2025
initialEvidence.text: Part: VA-220. Changes take effect from the first 2026 production run (12 Jan 2026): (1) the internal slide seal will come from Corlin Polymer instead of Ferrand Elastomers, at lower cost (Ferrand remains an approved source); (2) VA-220 assembly moves from Line 1 to the new Line 3. Validation: 30 Corlin seals checked for dimensions and hardness. The 100% end-of-line pressure-decay leak test on rig LT-04 is unchanged. Approved by the Brenmoor supplier quality engineer on 15 Dec 2025.

initialEvidence.source: Notes of call with Renata Oduya, Field Service Manager, 8 Oct 2026
initialEvidence.text: 'My techs are replacing more VA-220s on jobs done by the new installer firms. That's the pattern they report.' The new firms work mostly on new-build housing estates, so nearly all their installs are 2026-built units. Legacy firms do more replacements of older stock. She also flagged firmware 4.2 (over-the-air from 10 Mar), which cut minimum compressor off-time from 180 s to 90 s, 'so more valve shifts'. Units without the connectivity module (about a quarter) stay on 4.1. She has not formally split failures by installer or by firmware.

initialEvidence.source: Pellacott certificate of conformance, lot P26-0731, as uploaded to the SupplierPath portal
initialEvidence.text: Part VA-220, lot P26-0731, quantity 800, build date 21 Jul 2026. Test: 100% pressure-decay leak test at 24 bar, limit 5.0 Pa/min, rig LT-04 (calibration due 30 Nov 2026). Per-piece results table attached (800 values), range 0.6–1.9 Pa/min; 800/800 pass. Operator: K.D. Signed: S. Mirek, Quality Manager. Shipment paperwork carries only a one-line lot pass statement. Per-piece certificates are uploaded to the portal in batches for SupplierPath document review.

catalogue.title: Installer onboarding and training records, firms onboarded Feb–Apr 2026
catalogue.text: All 14 installer firms added Feb–Apr 2026 completed Brenmoor's 3-day AH-series certification: refrigerant handling, brazing with nitrogen purge, evacuation to 500 microns, commissioning. Spot audits of first installs: 11 firms had no findings; 3 firms had one minor finding each (incomplete commissioning checklist ×2, missing evacuation printout ×1). New firms installed about 35% of 2026 AH-series units. Legacy firms over the same period: 4 minor findings across 31 firms.

catalogue.title: Firmware 4.2 change record and validation summary, March 2026
catalogue.text: Change record FW-4.2, approved 2 Mar 2026, over-the-air rollout from 10 Mar. Change: minimum compressor off-time cut from 180 s to 90 s to improve comfort at low load; defrost logic unchanged. Expected effect: about 15% more compressor starts per day in shoulder seasons. Reversing-valve shifts happen at defrost entry and exit and at heating/cooling mode changes. Validation: 6 lab units, 1,200 h accelerated cycling, no valve faults. Units without a connectivity module cannot receive the update and remain on 4.1.

catalogue.title: SupplierPath on-site audit reports for Pellacott, Q2 and Q3 2026
catalogue.text: Q2 audit on site 2 Jul (announced 20 Jun); Q3 audit 30 Sep (announced 12 Sep). Auditor: Brenmoor SQE. Checklist sections: document control, training, 5S, calibration records, traceability, test-record review. Q3 findings: calibration certificates on file for LT-01 to LT-04, all in date; VA-220 test records 'complete, all lots 100% pass'. Line 3 VA-220 was not running on either audit day ('changeover to HX-3 build'), so the end-of-line test was not witnessed. Minor findings: two unsigned training records; one faded gauge label.

catalogue.title: Pellacott written response to Brenmoor warranty concern, 6 Oct 2026
catalogue.source: S. Mirek, Quality Manager, Pellacott Precision
catalogue.text: 'Every VA-220 shipped in 2026 was 100% pressure-decay tested on LT-04 against the 5.0 Pa/min limit and passed; the certificates are on your portal. Our SupplierPath score reflects this discipline. Our experience with other customers suggests VA-220 internal leakage usually comes from overheating during brazing or moisture from poor evacuation. We recommend Brenmoor review its new installers' practices. We are happy to supply fresh certificates for any held lots.'

catalogue.title: Brenmoor quality-lab memo: VA-220 teardown, warehouse retest and claim breakdown, October 2026
catalogue.text: 1. Teardown of 41 returned VA-220s (all Pellacott, built Feb–Jul 2026): 38 show internal seat leakage with the slide seal deformed and unseated. Brazed joints and external fittings intact on all 41. 2. Helium leak retest of warehouse valves that were never installed or powered: Pellacott 2026-built lots, 44 of 400 leak at the seat (11%); Pellacott 2025-built, 1 of 100; Durrant-Hale, 0 of 100. Pellacott's pressure-decay method was not replicated. 3. Claims within 120 days per 1,000 units, Feb–May builds. With Pellacott 2026 valves: legacy installers 41, new installers 42; firmware 4.1 units 40, 4.2 units 42. With Durrant-Hale valves: 5–7 in every installer and firmware group. 4. Seal compound not analysed. Every 2026 sample has both the Corlin seal and Line 3 assembly, so the two cannot be separated.

catalogue.title: Field technician pulse survey, free-text comments, September 2026
catalogue.text: 23 of 61 technicians responded. Selected comments: 'New-build jobs from the new firms are a mess — vacuum not pulled long enough.' 'Swapped three valves on one estate in a week, all new-installer jobs.' 'Valves come out looking clean, no burn marks, which is odd for a braze problem.' 'Since the update the units click over more often in mild weather.' 'Old firms aren't perfect either.' No survey question asked about part source or build date.

catalogue.title: Warranty claim portal migration notes, April 2026
catalogue.text: Claims moved from emailed forms to the new ServiceLink portal on 6 Apr 2026. Claim codes are now chosen from a drop-down list rather than typed. Post-migration check: 200 claims re-coded by hand, 94% agreement with the portal code. Claim volume per installed unit for non-valve codes changed by less than 5% across the migration.

catalogue.title: SupplierPath programme scores, all 22 suppliers, Q4 2025–Q3 2026
catalogue.text: Average overall score went from 74 to 86. Test-record conformance component: average 71 to 96; 19 of 22 suppliers at 95 or above by Q3. On-site process audit component: average 75 to 78. Suppliers with dock-to-stock status: 3 to 15. Pellacott's gain is within the programme's range (largest gain +23, Tanvik Fasteners). The programme does not collect rig logs or raw test files from any supplier.

catalogue.title: Purchasing records: Pellacott VA-220 contract terms and volumes, 2025–2026
catalogue.text: Contract renewed 5 Jan 2026: unit price cut 4% in exchange for Pellacott's VA-220 share rising from 70% to 80%. A new clause pays Pellacott a 1.5% rebate if it reaches dock-to-stock by Q3 2026 (reached in July; rebate paid in August). Monthly VA-220 volume is about 3,300 units. Durrant-Hale holds a 20% share at a unit price 6% above Pellacott's.

catalogue.title: Calibration contractor site-visit report, Pellacott leak-test rigs, 8 October 2026
catalogue.source: Metrova Calibration Ltd, engaged by Brenmoor under supply-agreement clause 9.4
catalogue.text: Rig LT-04 found disconnected and tagged 'OUT OF SERVICE – pressure transducer failed 9 Jan 2026'. LT-04 controller memory: last test cycle 18 Dec 2025. Controller logs for rigs LT-01 to LT-03 show only part families HX-1 and HX-3 in 2026; no VA-220 test program is loaded on them. No other leak-test equipment on site. At Brenmoor's request we compared the per-piece tables in 31 of Pellacott's 36 VA-220 certificates dated 2026. Every table matches, value for value, one of four sequences, and the same sequences appear in Pellacott certificates from November 2025. Pellacott's quality manager said the VA-220 was 'tested on a backup rig'. No backup rig was shown and no log of one was produced.

catalogue.title: Corlin Polymer seal material datasheet and PPAP summary
catalogue.text: Compound CP-HNBR-70. Datasheet: hardness 70 ±5 Shore A; compression set (22 h at 150 °C) of 25% or less; compatible with R-32 and POE oil. PPAP to Pellacott (Nov 2025): 30 seals checked for dimensions and hardness, all conforming. Compression set and refrigerant-oil immersion results are stated 'per datasheet' and were not tested on production lots. Ferrand Elastomers' previous compound was HNBR at 75 Shore A.

catalogue.title: Heating degree-day data, winter 2025–26 against five-year average
catalogue.text: November 2025 to March 2026: heating degree-days 4% above the five-year average. April to June 2026: 2% below. Regional variation within ±6% of the national figure. The coldest month was January 2026. No unusual cold spells were recorded in the AH-series' main sales regions.

catalogue.title: Interview notes: Brenmoor supplier quality engineer for Pellacott, 14 Oct 2026
catalogue.text: 'Pellacott went from our worst paperwork to our best in one quarter, with full per-piece tables on every lot. I approved the PCN because the seal was dimensionally fine and the leak test wasn't changing. On audit days the VA-220 never seemed to be running; they said they batch it on nights. I didn't ask for rig logs because SupplierPath doesn't require them. Dock-to-stock was automatic once they hit 85.'

catalogue.title: Customer complaints sample, AH-series, Aug–Sep 2026
catalogue.text: 25 complaints sampled. 18 report loss of heating or 'blowing cool air in heat mode'; 4 report noise; 3 report app connectivity problems. 9 mention the installer favourably and 5 unfavourably. Average time from installation to complaint: 4.5 months. None of the complaints identifies the valve supplier.

catalogue.title: Brenmoor receiving inspection records, Pellacott VA-220, Jan–Oct 2026
catalogue.text: Jan–Jun: per lot, visual and dimensional check on 5 pieces plus a check that a certificate is present. No leak testing at receiving (not in the inspection plan since 2022). 0 rejections. Jul–Sep: dock-to-stock, no receiving checks. 1 Oct: receiving supervisor put six lots on hold after a warranty review meeting; the lots remain in the bonded area.

hypotheses.text: Installation errors by the installer firms onboarded in 2026 caused the rise in VA-220 field failures.
Pellacott's VA-220 valves built in 2026 are defective, and the leak-test certificates Pellacott submitted for them do not reflect tests that were actually performed.
Pellacott's VA-220 valves built in 2026 are defective, and Pellacott performed the leak tests its certificates record, but that test method does not detect the defect.
Firmware 4.2's shorter minimum compressor off-time caused the rise in VA-220 field failures.
Other SupplierPath suppliers have also submitted test records that do not reflect tests that were actually performed.

edges.from: Defects in Pellacott VA-220 valves built in 2026
Onboarding of new installer firms in 2026
Pellacott's switch of slide-seal source to Corlin Polymer
Pellacott's submitted test records becoming complete, with every piece shown within the leak limit

actions.text: Quarantine all 2026-built Pellacott VA-220 stock (including the six held lots), suspend Pellacott's dock-to-stock status, and release VA-220 stock only after Brenmoor-run helium leak testing.
Suspend the certification of the 14 installer firms onboarded in 2026 and charge their VA-220 warranty claims back to them.
Release the six held VA-220 lots to production once Pellacott supplies fresh certificates of conformance for them.
Instruct Pellacott to go back to Ferrand Elastomers as the slide-seal source for all VA-220 production.
Change SupplierPath scoring so that submitted test records earn credit only when backed by rig logs or a witnessed test, starting from the next audit cycle.
